_comment: Hand-corrected layouts: classes where the recovered type is demonstrably wrong about a
member's TYPE, with the evidence for each written down beside it. Offsets and sizeof are
never changed here - only how the bytes at a known offset are spelled - and merge_layouts
refuses an entry whose size disagrees with the one already recorded.
This is the narrowest of the layout sources and should stay that way. An inference belongs in
layouts_from_*.json, a recovered type in layouts_kit.json; this file is only for a reading
taken directly out of the binary that contradicts both.

evidence: The IDB type gives dword0/dwordC/gap24[128] - correct offsets, no types - so the fields at
0x18 and 0x1C came out u32 when they hold floats, and everything from 0x24 came out as two
opaque byte arrays.
0x18: ?SetActuatorValue@vehFeedback@@UAEHHM@Z at 0x004D57F0 is
*(float *)&this[a2 + 6] = a3;   this[a2 + 4] = Timer::Ticks();
with a2 bounded by `a2 <= 1`. this[a2+6] is 0x18 + 4*a2 and this[a2+4] is 0x10 + 4*a2, so
0x18 is two floats and 0x10 is the two Timers already recorded.
0x24: ?PlayFeedbackSample@vehFeedback@@UAEHHHPAMPAH@Z at 0x004D5830 indexes
so the region is TWO 132-byte blocks, and 0x24 + 2*132 = 0x12C, the size the binary
allocates. Within a block at base B it writes 4*v9+36 -> B+0x00 (the f32* argument),
4*v9+68 -> B+0x20 (the i32* argument), 4*v9+100 -> B+0x40 (the i32 argument),
128*a2+132+4*v5 -> B+0x60, and increments *((_DWORD *)v6 + 41) -> B+0x80. v5 is a free-slot
index found by scanning B+0x00 and capped at 8, which is what fixes each array at 8 entries.
The constructor at 0x004D56C0 agrees independently: its loop runs 8 times at stride 4 over
the eight bases 0x24, 0x44, 0x64, 0x84, 0xA8, 0xC8, 0xE8 and 0x108, writing -1 to 0x84 and
0x108 - the two SampleState arrays - and 0 to the rest.
Flat per-channel arrays rather than a nested struct only because layouts.json cannot express
one; the offsets are what the still-assembly code actually reads.
NAMES CORRECTED AFTER READING GetNextUnit at 0x004D5980, which is the only function that
consumes these arrays rather than filling them. What PlayFeedbackSample stores looked like an
id and a state flag; GetNextUnit shows otherwise:
v7 = SamplePos[slot]; SamplePos[slot] = v7 + 1;      a per-sample CURSOR, not a flag
if ( v7 < SampleLength[slot] ) ...                   the third array is a LENGTH
value = SampleValues[slot][v7]                       both pointers are indexed BY it
label = SampleLabels[slot][v7]
and when the cursor reaches the length the slot is released - values and labels nulled, length
0, cursor back to -1, count decremented. The constructor's -1 and PlayFeedbackSample's 0 are
therefore a free marker and a start position, which is consistent with both.
ctor ??0mmPositions@@QAE@XZ at 0x0052A0B0 is 0xD bytes and writes exactly three slots,
0x0, 0x4 and 0x8, all to zero. Nothing in the class touches anything above 0xB.
0x0 is a heap pointer: the dtor at 0x0052A0C0 is `operator delete(*this); *this = 0;`
and ?Init@mmPositions@@QAEXH@Z at 0x0052A0E0 is
pvVar1 = operator_new(param_1 * 4);  *(int *)(this + 8) = param_1;
*(void **)this = pvVar1;
so 0x0 is an allocated array of 4-byte elements and 0x8 is the requested count.
?GetVector4@ at 0x0052A310 indexes it as *(int *)(*(int *)this + param_1 * 4), i.e. an
array of pointers.
0x4 is the live count: ?GetCount@mmPositions@@QAEHXZ at 0x0052A300 is exactly
`return *(int *)(this + 4);` - the name is the mangled name of its own getter, not a
guess - and ?Register@ at 0x0052A410 does
if (*(int *)(this + 4) == *(int *)(this + 8)) return -1;
then post-increments 0x4, which is what fixes 0x8 as the capacity.
0x8 + 4 = 12, and data/measured_sizes.json independently measures 12.
ctor ??0Aud3DAmbientObject@@QAE@XZ at 0x005150A0 calls Aud3DObject::Aud3DObject(this)
first, so [0x0, 0x60) is the base - Aud3DObject is 0x60 and already check_size-verified.
It then writes 0x60, 0x64, 0x6C, 0x70, 0x74, 0x78 and 0x7C as dwords and 0x68, 0x69 as
BYTES, with 0x70 set to 1065353216 = 1.0f.
0x60 is the element count and 0x7C the array it counts: the dtor at 0x005150E0 is
for (i = 0; i < *(_DWORD *)(this + 96); ++i)
operator delete(*(void **)(*(_DWORD *)(this + 124) + 4 * i));
then deletes the array itself, so 0x7C is an owned array of pointers.
?GetSoundDataPtr@Aud3DAmbientObject@@QAEPAUtagAud3DAmbientSoundData@@H@Z returns
*(tagAud3DAmbientSoundData **)(*(int *)(this + 0x7c) + param_1 * 4) - the mangled return
type names the element type outright.
0x6C, 0x70, 0x74 and 0x78 are floats by use: 0x6C multiplies into AudSoundBase::SetVolume,
and 0x78 appears in a float range test against param_1+0x14 and param_1+0x18.
0x68 and 0x69 are byte flags, written as bytes and tested as `this[0x68] == 0`.
The highest offset referenced by any of the class's 30 recovered functions is 0x7C, so
0x7C + 4 = 0x80. aiSubwayAudio, which derives from this class, starts its own field at
0x80 - the two agree.
THE BASE IS Aud3DAmbientObject (0x80), NOT Aud3DObject (0x60). The ctor
??0aiSubwayAudio@@QAE@XZ at 0x0059D660 calls Aud3DAmbientObject::Aud3DAmbientObject at
this+0; the dtor at 0x0059D680 calls Aud3DAmbientObject::~Aud3DAmbientObject; and
?Activate@ / ?Deactivate@ at 0x0059D690 / 0x0059D6D0 call
Aud3DAmbientObject::ActivateSound((Aud3DAmbientObject *)this, i).
The ctor is 0x20 bytes and writes only the vptr and *(int *)(this + 0x80) = 0.
?Update@aiSubwayAudio@@QAEXM@Z at 0x0059D710 reads and writes that slot as a two-state
selector:
if (*(int *)(this + 0x80) == 1) { Deactivate(1); Activate(0); ... = 0; }
a 4-byte compare and store. Nothing references anything above 0x83.
0x80 + 4 = 0x84, and aiSubway (0x14C) records this class embedded at 0xC8 with width 132:
0xC8 + 0x84 = 0x14C exactly. This entry is useless without Aud3DAmbientObject, since
without it the base collapses to 0x60 and the class comes out 0x64.
ctor ??0aiCableCarAudioData@@QAE@XZ at 0x0059E2B0 writes DWORD indices 0 through 12,
i.e. offsets 0x00 to 0x30 inclusive, and nothing beyond. 0x30 + 4 = 0x34.
The first five slots are named by their own getters' mangled names, so these are recovered
names rather than invented ones: ?GetGoPtr@ at 0x0059E380 returns *(AudSoundBase **)this,
?GetStopPtr@ at 0x0059E390 returns this+4, ?GetLoopPtr@ at 0x0059E3A0 returns this+8,
?GetGetSpeedPtr@ at 0x0059E3B0 returns this+0xC and ?GetCrossIntersectionPtr@ at
0x0059E3C0 returns this+0x10. Each mangled return type is PAVAudSoundBase.
?AssignSounds@ at 0x0059E630 pairs the sample ids at 0x18/0x1C/0x20/0x24/0x28 into the
pointers at 0x00/0x04/0x08/0x0C/0x14 via GetSample, and ?UnAssignSounds@ at 0x0059E6A0
clears 0x14 alongside 0x00-0x0C. 0x10 is zeroed by the ctor and never assigned - the
CrossIntersection slot is dead in retail.
The ids at 0x18-0x28 are Aud3DObjectManager::AllocateSample results for the named samples
CABLECARGOBELL, CABLECARSTOP, CABLECAR, CABLECARSTART and STREETCABLE. Which sound a slot
holds is not a field name, so those keep field_ names.
0x2C is a state: ?UpdateState@ at 0x0059E580 assigns 0..3 and ?UpdatePlay@ at 0x0059E3D0
switches on it, then mirrors it into 0x30 as the previous state.
ctor ??0aiCableCarAudio@@QAE@XZ at 0x0059D350 calls Aud3DObject::Aud3DObject(this), so
[0x0, 0x60) is the base, then constructs aiCableCarAudioData in place at this+104 (0x68).
The base is confirmed by use rather than merely asserted: ?Init@ at 0x0059D400 writes
*(undefined4 *)(this + 0x40) = 8, which is Aud3DObject::Priority at 0x40, and the inlined
Reset at 0x0059D440 touches 0x4, 0x8, 0xC, 0x10, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x2C, 0x30, 0x44 and
0x48 - every one a named Aud3DObject field at its recorded offset.
?Init@aiCableCarAudio@@QAEXPAVVector3@@PAM@Z at 0x0059D400 does
*(float **)(this + 0x60) = param_2;   *(float *)(this + 100) = *param_2;
so 0x60 holds the float* (PAM in the mangled name) and 0x64 a cached copy of its pointee.
?UpdateAudio@ at 0x0059D460 confirms both:
*(undefined4 *)(this + 100) = **(undefined4 **)(this + 0x60);
and 0x0059D490 passes them to UpdateState as the current and previous value.
0x68 + sizeof(aiCableCarAudioData) = 0x68 + 0x34 = 0x9C = 156, and aiCableCar (0x184)
already records this class embedded at 0xE8 with width 156: 0xE8 + 0x9C = 0x184 exactly.

members.name: field_68
members.src: ctor constructs in place at this+104

evidence: ctor ??0aiAmbientVehicleAudio@@QAE@XZ at 0x004CF890 calls Aud3DObject::Aud3DObject(this),
so [0x0, 0x60) is the base, then writes exactly thirteen slots: 0x60, 0x64, 0x68 and 0x6C
to -1; 0x70, 0x74, 0x78, 0x7C, 0x80 and 0x84 to 0 as dwords; and 0x88, 0x89 to 0 as BYTES.
The four -1 slots are container indices, each filled by its own loader through an int*
out-param and then used to index a manager array - ?LoadHorn@ at 0x004D0300 takes
this+0x60, ?LoadEngine@ at 0x004D00D0 takes this+100, ?LoadVoices@ at 0x004D0530 takes
this+0x68 and ?LoadImpacts@ at 0x004D07B0 takes this+0x6C; AssignSounds at 0x004CF9D0 then
reads s_ppHornAudioContainer[*(int *)(this + 0x60)] and its three counterparts, the
AudCreature one guarded by != -1 against the ctor's sentinel.
The four pointer slots are typed by the callee class in the machine code, not inferred:
?GetAudImpactPtr@...@@QAEPAVAudImpact@@XZ at 0x004CFB10 is literally
`return *(AudImpact **)(this + 0x70);`; 0x74 is passed to vehHornAudio::Update; 0x78 to
AudCreature::UpdateAttenuation/EchoOn/EchoOff; 0x7C to aiEngineAudio::UpdateDoppler and
CalculatePitch.
0x80 and 0x84 are floats - UpdateAudio at 0x004CFB90 evaluates
*(float *)(this + 0x84) - *(float *)(this + 0x80) <= 4.0 and *(float *)(this + 0x84) *= 0.95.
0x88 is a one-shot load latch (?Init@ at 0x004CF8F0 tests it then sets it to 1) and 0x89 an
echo flag (?EchoOn@ 0x004CFFE0 sets it, ?EchoOff@ 0x004D0030 clears it).
No recovered function of the class references any offset above 0x89, so the extent is 0x8A
and pads to 0x8C at align 4. aiVehicleSpline (0x18C) independently records this class
embedded at 0x100 with width 140: 0x100 + 0x8C = 0x18C. Two derivations, one answer.
THE 16 BYTES AT 0x18 ARE ATTESTED, NOT PROVEN, which is why this entry is PARTIAL while
the others recovered alongside it are CONFIRMED. No recovered function reads or writes
anything in [0x18, 0x28). What raises it above a guess is that the IDB type library records
the hole explicitly (_ALL_TYPES.h:47996 gives dgUnhitBangerInstance, char[16] gap at 0x18,
Matrix34 at 0x28) and both siblings show the same shape - dgHitBangerInstance is already in
the tree at 0x58 with a gap at 0x18 and a Matrix34 at 0x28, and passes check_size.
The size is certain: ?SizeOf@dgUnhitMtxBangerInstance@@UAEIXZ at 0x00442AF0 returns 0x58,
and dgUnhitBangerInstance::RequestBanger at 0x00441D80 calls lvlInstance::operator_new(0x58)
before storing this class's vftable pointer.
The Matrix34 at 0x28 is proven three ways:
?SetMatrix@ at 0x00441FD0 copies twelve dwords to this+0x28 - 48 bytes,
?GetMatrix@ at 0x00441FF0 returns (Matrix34 *)(this + 0x28),
?GetPosition@ at 0x00442000 returns (Vector3 *)(this + 0x4c), and 0x28 + 36 = 0x4C is the
matrix's fourth row - which fixes it as a Matrix34 rather than an opaque 48-byte blob.
0x28 + 0x30 = 0x58. The base dgUnhitBangerInstance adds nothing over dgBangerInstance
(0x18, check_size-verified in the tree), so 0x18 + 16 + 48 = 0x58.
The recovered entry is _D3DMATERIAL7 wearing gfxMaterial's name: five anonymous unions
IDA spells `union _D3DMATERIAL7::$F37024B6...`, which is not a C++ type, so only field_44
survived and the class compiled to 4 bytes against a required 0x48.
?Reset@gfxMaterial@@QAEXXZ at 0x004B1BB0 writes every byte of the class and fixes the whole
layout. It stores 0x3F800000 - 1.0f - to 0x00 through 0x1C, eight consecutive dwords, then
zero to 0x20 through 0x40, then:
*(undefined4 *)(this + 0x44) = 0xffffffff;
an INTEGER immediate, not a float, so 0x44 is a packed colour and not a fifth vector
component. 0xFFFFFFFF is opaque white, the identity for a modulated vertex colour.
sizeof is 0x48 and not the 0x44 of D3DMATERIAL7:
?AddStaticMaterial@modShader@@SAPAUgfxMaterial@@ABU2@@Z at 0x004A3930 does
pgVar2 = operator_new(DAT_005c9d98 * 0x48);
and strides the array by 0x48. A D3DMATERIAL7 is 0x44 - four D3DCOLORVALUE at 16 plus a
4-byte power - so gfxMaterial is that struct plus the colour word at 0x44, which is exactly
why the alias was close enough to be recorded and still wrong.
The four vector members and Shininess take their names from the D3DMATERIAL7 fields the
class mirrors and passes to SetMaterial - diffuse, ambient, specular, emissive, power - and
MM2Hook's own header agrees on all five. Color is named for its use, not from a symbol.
Spelled u32 rather than a ColorARGB type: the recovery of ColorARGB carries an IDA
anonymous-union member typed `$0457258C...` that cannot be declared, and the packed word is
fully described by its width here.
0x24 = 36 bytes, confirmed two ways. The kit records `union MM2::eqEvent // sizeof=0x24`
at _ALL_TYPES.h:48110 as a `MM2::eqEvent::data` overlaid with `char[36] buffer`, where
eqEvent::data (:48116) is nine ints, p0 through p8, at 0x00 to 0x20.
The binary agrees independently. ?Queue@eqEventQ@@AAEXAATeqEvent@@@Z at 0x004A3630 copies
the event with
for (iVar2 = 9; iVar2 != 0; iVar2 = iVar2 + -1) { *puVar3 = *(undefined4 *)param_1; ... }
- exactly NINE dwords - into a slot addressed as
*(int *)(this + 0xc) + uVar1 * 0x24
and ?Pop@eqEventQ@@QAEHPATeqEvent@@@Z at 0x004A3670 strides the same array by 0x24.
SPELLED AS ONE ARRAY MEMBER, NOT NINE SCALARS. A union's members all sit at offset 0, so a
nine-member list would tile as an overlap and would compile to a four-byte union. One
i32[9] gives the right size and the right semantics: the event really is an opaque
parameter block, moved wholesale and never interpreted by the queue.
The names stay generic because they are generic. MM2Hook calls them p0..p8 and the copy
loop treats all nine identically - nothing in eqEventQ reads an individual field, so there
is no evidence in the binary for a meaning to attach to any of them.
It must be a UNION and not a struct: `T` is MSVC's mangling tag for a union, and every one
of the 38 signatures naming it - ?Action@uiWidget@@UAEXTeqEvent@@@Z among them - encodes
that tag. A struct would mangle `U` and the symbol would not match.
